# DOI re-pin — devlog-2026-11-10-novelty-scan.qmd, section 5 Source list

Date of verification: **2026-11-10**. Scope: every DOI-bearing entry in the
devlog's [M] source list (18 entries / 21 DOI strings), the extra [M]-class DOI
string cited in section 2 (E3, `10.1016/j.patrec.2007.09.010`), and the two
[U] entries carrying DOIs (`10.1186/gm1228`, `10.1093/bioinformatics/btab144`).

## Method note

- **Fetch strategy (two passes per DOI):**
  1. `https://doi.org/<doi>` resolved with `curl -L` (max 10 redirects,
     browser User-Agent); HTTP status, redirect count, and final publisher
     URL recorded, and the landing HTML saved for `<title>` /
     `citation_*` meta extraction.
  2. DOI content negotiation (`Accept:
     application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json`) through `https://doi.org/`
     — i.e., the publisher-deposited metadata record served by the DOI
     registration agency (Crossref transform endpoint) — parsed for title,
     container-title, issued year, first author.
- **Evidence classes.** `PAGE` = rendered publisher HTML retrieved and
  title/citation-meta read directly. `CN+REDIRECT` = the DOI resolved
  through the full redirect chain to the correct publisher article URL,
  and the publisher-deposited metadata record matches the cited work, but
  the final HTML was bot-gated (Cloudflare "Just a moment…", Incapsula
  "Client Challenge", or HTTP 429 at biorxiv) so the human-readable page
  could not be rendered. Under the honesty law no DOI was guessed or
  reconstructed from memory; corrections were located only via Crossref
  bibliographic search and then the corrected string itself re-resolved.
- **Verdict rules.** PINNED = resolved record (page and/or
  publisher-deposited metadata) matches the devlog's citation line on
  title, venue, and year. CORRECTED = listed DOI resolves to a different
  valid record or 404s, and a corrected DOI was found by search AND the
  corrected string itself resolved to a record matching the cited work.
  UNRESOLVED = could not be pinned to the cited work (404, bot-block with
  no usable record, or resolves to an unrelated work with no verified
  correction).

## Notes on evidence quality

- 4 entries were pinned from the rendered publisher page (`PAGE`): SUITOR
  (PLOS), MuSiCal (Nature Genetics), Medo (Nature Communications), SigFormer
  (bioRxiv).
- 16 entries were pinned via the DOI system's own content-negotiated,
  publisher-deposited metadata plus a completed redirect chain to the
  correct publisher article URL (`CN+REDIRECT`). Bot-gates encountered:
  Cloudflare managed challenge at academic.oup.com (403), Incapsula
  "Client Challenge" at link.springer.com / bmcbioinformatics /
  projecteuclid.org (HTTP 200 but challenge HTML), HTTP 429 at
  biorxiv.org, and an HTTP 403 at journals.sagepub.com. In every such
  case the redirect Location chain terminated at the correct article path
  on the publisher host, and the CN record matched the cited work —
  this is treated as sufficient for a pin, since the garble risk being
  tested (wrong/nonexistent DOI string) would manifest as a 404 or a
  mismatched record, neither of which occurred.
- Elsevier DOIs terminate at a `linkinghub.elsevier.com` JS redirect to
  ScienceDirect; the PII embedded in the redirect target plus the
  publisher-deposited CN record were used as confirmation.
- The extra `10.1016/j.patrec.2007.09.010` probe (row 22) was fetched
  because the devlog cites it in section 2 with a different journal
  fragment than section 5's `patcog` string — exactly the digits/separators
  drift class this re-pin was auditing; it resolved to an unrelated
  fingerprint-verification paper, confirming the drift, and the corrected
  `patcog` string (already listed in §5) was re-verified directly.

(merged as PR #96). That devlog marked three items pending or [U]-only; this
document is the formal targeted re-scan that upgrades or downgrades each:

   (MSU-LowCount) — "(a), pending formal scan."
2. **Claim 2 (devlog line 81):** CoDA/DM-mixture exposure association

Repo files were READ for context only. No file inside the repository was
created, modified, or deleted; all writes landed under `/tmp/noveltylane2/`.

## Method and provenance discipline

The house zero-fabrication law applies, unchanged from the parent scan. Every
source is tiered:

- **[P]** primary page fetched and read in this scan (arXiv abstract pages via
  curl with a browser User-Agent; publisher/bioRxiv HTML). Four arXiv records
  are [P]-verified at the abstract level: 2404.10974, 2502.01468, 2510.07518,
  2610.00523.
- **[M]** bibliographic metadata confirmed through search backends (OpenAlex
  REST API via curl, Crossref REST API via curl, `scholar_search`) — title +
  venue + DOI exactly as returned.
- **[U]** unverified in this scan — carried from the repo corpus or from
  model knowledge; never load-bearing for a verdict.

**DOI-garble caveat.** Search backends have exhibited systematic
digit/separator garble in DOI transcription. All DOIs below are transcribed
exactly as returned by the backend that surfaced them; none has been
re-pinned against the publisher page in this scan (that is a separate
exercise). The sibling deliverable
`/tmp/noveltylane2/doi-repin-2026-11-10.md` re-pinned the parent devlog's
source list the same day and empirically confirmed the garble class (one
`patrec`/`patcog` journal-fragment drift, one 404 DOI corrected to
`10.1093/bioinformatics/btad756`), so the caveat is not hypothetical.

**Backend reliability note.** `mcp__websearch__web_search` returned Chinese
dictionary entries for all four English queries (W1–W4) — unusable, results
discarded. The built-in `WebSearch` returned empty result sets for both
quoted queries (B1–B2). `mcp__websearch__scholar_search` (OpenAlex backend)
was reliable. The workhorse was `curl` against `api.openalex.org` and
`api.crossref.org`; arXiv `/abs/` pages fetched cleanly; `dash.harvard.edu`
was permanently bot-blocked (HTTP 429 via fetch_page; a 1515-byte bot-gated
stub via curl with full Chrome UA; HTTP 401 on the DASH REST API endpoint).

**Search-volume accounting.** 62 logged search/fetch tool invocations:
10 `scholar_search` + 4 `mcp__websearch__web_search` + 2 built-in
`WebSearch` + 1 `fetch_page` + 45 Bash curl-family network calls. Distinct
search operations: 59 (removing one duplicate curl pair C40/C41, one
non-search directory-creation call, and one log-extraction script run that
touched no network). The verbatim query log is embedded per claim below.

**Negative results are supportive, not conclusive.** Every per-claim verdict
below rests partly on searches that returned nothing relevant; search
backends index titles/abstracts, not full texts, and non-English or
tool-documentation venues are under-covered. A negative here lowers the
probability of prior art; it cannot zero it.

## Claim 1 — Conformal prediction for signature exposures (MSU-LowCount)

**Parent-scan status:** "(a), pending formal scan." This scan adjudicates it.

- scholar_search S01 `conformal prediction mutational signature exposure` · S02 `conformal prediction non-negative matrix factorization deconvolution prediction intervals` · S03 `Mondrian conformal prediction bioinformatics calibrated intervals` · S04 `uncertainty quantification mutational signature activity confidence interval cancer genomes` · S05 `Catherine Xue uncertainty quantification non-negative matrix factorization mutational signatures` · S06 `conformal prediction intervals source contribution estimation blind source separation` · S07 `Bayesian non-negative matrix factorization mutational signatures posterior credible intervals exposures`
- web_search W1 `conformal prediction mutational signature exposure interval cancer` and W2 `"conformal prediction" "mutational signature"` (both garbled, discarded) · built-in WebSearch B1 `"conformal prediction" "mutational signature" cancer exposure` and B2 `conformal prediction NMF deconvolution prediction intervals biology` (both empty) · fetch_page F1 `https://dash.harvard.edu/handle/1/41730990` (HTTP 429)
- Bash curl (OpenAlex/Crossref/DASH/arXiv): "conformal prediction mutational signature"; "conformal prediction signature exposure deconvolution cancer"; `title.search:` "Catherine Xue mutational"; "Robust Uncertainty Quantification Non-Negative Matrix Factorization Mutational Signatures"; "Wild Bootstrap Inference NMF Random Effects"; "conformal prediction spectral unmixing or NMF interval"; SimplexUQ; "coverage calibrated confidence interval signature refitting assignment mutational"; "conformal prediction cancer genome variants calibration"; DASH handles 1/41730990 + 1/42725950 + DASH API; arXiv 2404.10974, 2502.01468, 2510.07518, 2610.00523 (all [P]); BASCULE; SigProfilerAssignment; Senkin MSA; Medo comparison.

### Findings

- **Xue, Catherine (2025). "Robust Uncertainty Quantification for
  Non-Negative Matrix Factorization with Applications to Mutational
  Signatures Analysis." Harvard DASH dissertation.** OpenAlex
  W7126542226; no DOI; landing `https://dash.harvard.edu/handle/1/42725950`.
  **[M]** — abstract UNVERIFIED: DASH blocked every access route in this
  environment (fetch_page 429; curl full-Chrome-UA returned a 1515-byte
  bot-gated stub; DASH REST API 401). This is the single explicit
  unresolved nearest-neighbor: the title says "robust uncertainty
  quantification for NMF with applications to mutational signatures," which
  is compatible both with posterior/Bayesian UQ and with distribution-free
  intervals. Whether it touches conformal methods for exposures could not
  be established from here.
- **SimplexUQ (2026), arXiv 2610.00523, DOI 10.48550/arxiv.2610.00523 [P,
  abstract verified]:** "first benchmark and reproducible protocol for
  measuring this allocation problem on simplex-valued predictions; it
  compares existing conformal wrappers rather than proposing a new one."
  Twelve simplex tasks include spectral abundances and cell-type fractions
  — adjacent domains, **no mutational-signature application**. Its headline
  result validates the Mondrian choice generically: CIFAR-10 marginal
  coverage 0.900 but worst-stratum 0.542; Mondrian raises worst-stratum to
  0.886 and cuts max disparity 0.358 → 0.022.
- **Posterior-based UQ line (adjacent, not conformal):** Zito & Miller 2024,
  "Compressive Bayesian non-negative matrix factorization for mutational
  signatures analysis," arXiv 2404.10974 [P]; Hansen, Grabski, Parmigiani
  2025, Bayesian Probit Multi-Study NMF, arXiv 2502.01468 [P]; Hansen et
  al. 2025, Zero-Inflated Bayesian Multi-Study Infinite NMF, arXiv
  2510.07518 [P, dietary application]; Landy, Basava, Parmigiani 2026,
  "bayesNMF," JCGS, 10.1080/10618600.2026.2657487 [M]; sigfit, bioRxiv
  10.1101/372896 [M]; Hua et al. 2026, Ann Appl Stat, 10.1214/26-aoas2138
  [M]. All produce posterior/credible intervals from Bayesian models — a
  different guarantee class than distribution-free, coverage-audited
  conformal intervals.
- **MSA (Senkin et al. 2021), BMC Bioinformatics, 10.1186/s12859-021-04450-8
  [M]:** simulation-calibrated confidence for signature attribution — not
  conformal, not coverage-audited on real data.
- **Medo et al. 2024, Nat Commun, 10.1038/s41467-024-53711-6 [M]**
  (12-tool fit comparison; its open-question row corroborates the
  sub-100-mutation fitting gap) and **BASCULE 2025, Genome Biology,
  10.1186/s13059-025-03835-9 [M]** (credible intervals) — neither applies
  conformal wrappers.
- **Conformal-in-biomedicine is generic published art:** Papangelou et al.
  2025, Frontiers in Bioinformatics, 10.3389/fbinf.2025.1507448 [M];
  Sreenivasan et al. 2025, npj Digital Medicine, 10.1038/s41746-025-01616-z
  [M]; ACM Computing Surveys survey 10.1145/3736575 [M]. Mondrian conformal
  in chemistry/toxicology: CPSign 10.1186/s13321-024-00870-9 [M]; iSKIN
  10.1002/smm2.1278 [M]; eMolTox 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty135 [M];
  10.1016/j.xphs.2020.09.055 [M]. No instance found in any of these domains
  of conformal intervals for mixture-deconvolution exposures.
- **Negative search:** OpenAlex queries pairing "conformal" with
  "mutational signature" / "signature exposure" / "deconvolution" /
  "source contribution" / "spectral unmixing" returned zero records
  applying conformal prediction to signature (or analogous mixture) exposures.

### Verdict recommendation: (a) genuinely novel — with one named caveat

Reasoning: conformal methodology itself is published art (Shafer–Vovk,
Angelopoulos–Bates, and the biomedicine/chem applications above); the
novelty claim reduces to the *application* — Mondrian-by-TMB-stratum
conformal intervals for signature exposures with verified empirical
coverage on stratified simulations and retrospective real panel data. No
prior art surfaced that does this. Differentiation from the nearest
neighbors: SimplexUQ benchmarks generic simplex conformal wrappers but
never touches signatures; the Bayesian-NMF line delivers posterior
intervals, not distribution-free coverage guarantees; MSA is
simulation-calibrated, not coverage-audited. The Xue 2025 dissertation is
the one record that could conceivably overlap and could not be inspected
beyond metadata — it must be read (it is a public dissertation) before the
(a) is printed in the manuscript. **Negative results here are supportive,
not conclusive:** backend coverage of dissertations and of tool
documentation is weak, and the Xue caveat is unresolved.

## Claim 2 — CoDA methodology for signature-exposure association (MSU-Infer)

**Parent-scan status:** "(b)"; the "first exposure-association framework
covering survival/case-control/longitudinal" phrasing was deferred to this
scan.

### Query log (Claim 2)

- scholar_search S08 `compositional data analysis mutational signature exposure association Dirichlet multinomial` · S09 `Morrill mutational signature association analysis compositional` · S10 `differential mutational process association case control log-ratio CLR tumor signatures statistics` · web_search W3 `Morrill 2025 mutational signatures compositional data association survival arxiv` (garbled, discarded)
- Bash curl (OpenAlex): "compositional data analysis cancer mutation spectra log-ratio signature activity"; "Dirichlet multinomial mixed model differential abundance mutational signatures"; "Morrill mutational signatures"; DOI lookup 10.1186/s12859-025-06055-x; log-ratio compositional survival/Cox; SurvBal / FLORAL / coda4microbiome / Cox-compositional; Diffsig; Morrison SVA; Hart AMSD; "compositional data mutational signature exposures ILR CLR associations".

### Findings

- **Morrill et al. 2025, "A Dirichlet-multinomial mixed model for
  determining differential abundance of mutational signatures," BMC
  Bioinformatics, 10.1186/s12859-025-06055-x [M, full abstract via
  OpenAlex]:** paired design (two observations per patient), multivariate
  random effects, group-specific dispersion, regression generalization;
  validated on PCAWG clonal/subclonal data; ~0 citations at scan time.
  This is CoDA-adjacent DM modeling for signature DA **including a
  regression generalization** — the closest single competitor.
- **Diffsig (Park, Smith, Van Alsten 2024), "Diffsig: Associating Risk
  Factors with Mutational Signatures," Cancer Epidemiology Biomarkers &
  Prevention, 10.1158/1055-9965.epi-23-0728 [M]:** risk-factor association
  testing on signature exposures that "takes into account the uncertainty
  associated with assigning signatures to samples." Case-control-class
  association testing in signature space already exists.
- **Hart, Alcala, Feder, Harris (2026), "A signature-agnostic test for
  differences between tumor mutation spectra reveals carcinogen and
  ancestry effects," 10.1038/s42003-026-09652-5 [M; DOI prefix =
  Communications Biology class; venue string not separately
  page-pinned]:** AMSD permutation test — group comparison of mutation
  spectra without fitting signatures. Abstract as returned: "Despite
  dozens of tools to identify mutational signatures in cancer samples,
  there is not an established metric for quantifying whether signature
  expo[sures differ]" (truncated by backend).
- **Morrison et al. 2023 (bioRxiv preprint, 10.1101/2023.11.23.23298821
  [M]):** signature variability analysis (SVA), population-genetics
  statistics on signature diversity/homogeneity vs carcinogen exposure —
  exposure-phenotype association, non-CoDA machinery.
- **The CoDA-survival / CoDA-case-control methodology exists maturely — in
  microbiome, not signatures:** SurvBal, Bioinformatics 2024,
  10.1093/bioinformatics/btae612 [M]; balance-based differential
  abundance, NAR Genom Bioinform 2024, 10.1093/nargab/lqae038 [M]; FLORAL,
  Cell Reports Methods 2024, 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100899 [M];
  coda4microbiome R package, 10.32614/cran.package.coda4microbiome [M];
  Cox regression on log-ratio transformed compositional data, Stat Med /
  10.1177/0962280219864125 [M]. No record found porting any of these to
  mutational-signature exposures.
- **Negative search:** queries combining CLR/ILR/log-ratio/Dirichlet-
  multinomial with "mutational signature" + survival / case-control /
  longitudinal surfaced only the five records above — nothing that spans
  all three outcome types in signature space.

### Verdict recommendation: (b) novel combination — the "first" phrasing must be narrowed

Reasoning: every methodological ingredient exists. DM mixed modeling with
paired designs and regression generalization exists (Morrill 2025 —
devlog's plan is to reproduce then extend it, which is consistent with a
(b)); risk-factor association with assignment uncertainty exists (Diffsig
2024); group-comparison testing exists (Hart 2026, Morrison 2023); and
CoDA-survival/Cox-log-ratio machinery exists in microbiome. What did not
surface is a **unified exposure-association framework in signature space
covering survival, case-control, and longitudinal designs** — that is a
combination claim, not a first-in-class claim. Recommended manuscript
phrasing: "first CoDA-based framework for signature-exposure association
spanning survival, case-control, and longitudinal designs in mutational-
signature space" — and even that only after checking Morrill 2025's cited-by
list again at submission time (it was 0 at scan date; a fast-moving
neighbor). **Negative results are supportive, not conclusive.**

## Claim 3 — TSB/RTT reporting + treatment/timing deconvolution

**Parent-scan status:** "near-zero competition" claim carried [U] from
`docs/research/00` §2 post-processing; ordered to be scanned before printing
"first." **The scan REFUTES the note for the TSB/RTT half.** Split verdict:

### Query log (Claim 3)

- web_search W4 `N-of-1-time MutationalPatterns relative timing of mutational processes single sample` (garbled, discarded)
- Bash curl (OpenAlex/Crossref): "transcriptional strand bias mutational signatures replication timing"; "strand bias mutation signature transcription asymmetry cancer tool"; "per-sample transcriptional strand bias signature attribution reporting tool asymmetry per signature"; TensorSignatures; "Accounting Transcriptional Asymmetries Mutational Signature Compressive Bayesian" (Zito chapter); TrackSig; "N-of-1-time mutational patterns timing signatures"; quoted "N-of-1-time" (OpenAlex, then Crossref); MutationalPatterns (both papers); "treatment associated mutational signature change longitudinal therapy response signature dynamics"; "chemotherapy platinum signature emergence treatment deconvolution sequential samples"; Blood 2023 tracking; "Timing the Initiation of Multiple Myeloma"; oesophageal dynamics; colorectal geographic/age variation Nature 2025; "mutational signatures treatment timing platinum temozolomide when acquired clinical"; "CLOCK mutational clock signature exposures shares separating SBS1 SBS5 time"; "clock signature shares SBS1 SBS5 separation tumor age attribute"; "extraction of timing information mutational signatures cancer genome subclonal clonal stratification tool"; "relative timing of mutational processes split catalog subclonal clonal single sample"; "relative timing mutational processes single sample R package"; chemotherapy-signature-timing-deconvolution query.

### Findings — half 1: per-signature TSB / RTT reporting

Substantial prior art exists; "near-zero competition" is **refuted** here:

- **TensorSignatures** (Jin et al. 2021?), "Learning mutational signatures
  and their multidimensional genomic properties with TensorSignatures,"
  Nature Communications, 10.1038/s41467-021-23551-9 [M]: joint learning of
  signatures with transcriptional/replication-strand and
  replication-timing covariates.
- **Bergstrom-line 2018**, "Mutational signature distribution varies with
  DNA replication timing and strand asymmetry," Genome Biology,
  10.1186/s13059-018-1509-y [M].
- **"Topography of mutational signatures in human cancer," Cell Reports
  2023, 10.1016/j.celrep.2023.112930 [M].**
- **SigProfilerTopography (NEW hit this session):** "Evaluating topography
  of mutational signatures with SigProfilerTopography," Genome Biology
  2025, 10.1186/s13059-025-03612-8 [M] — a maintained SigProfiler-family
  tool whose entire purpose is per-signature topographic (strand, timing,
  genomic-region) reporting.
- **Zito, Xue, Miller 2025**, "Accounting for Transcriptional Asymmetries
  in Mutational Signature Analysis Using Compressive Bayesian Non-negative
  Matrix Factorization," Springer chapter, 10.1007/978-3-031-96033-8_81
  [M] — strand asymmetry modeled inside the NMF likelihood.
- Supporting adjacency: RT-in-normal signatures 10.1038/s41598-023-34631-9
  [M]; SBS8 late-replication, Comm Biol 2020, 10.1038/s42003-020-01119-5
  [M]; MutationalPackages ecosystem 10.1186/s13073-018-0539-0 +
  10.1186/s12864-022-08357-3 [M] (strand-bias functions documented [U]
  from tool docs, not backend-surfaced).

**Verdict for the reporting half: (c) prior art for the capability; at most
(b) for a per-sample, per-signature reporting/UX combination inside a
refitting pipeline.** No "first" wording is defensible for TSB/RTT
reporting as such.

### Findings — half 2: treatment/timing deconvolution from mutation catalogs

Prior art is application-level, not a general tool — plausibly (b):

- **"Tracking the Evolution of Therapy-Related Myeloid Neoplasms Using
  Chemotherapy Signatures," Blood 2023, 10.1182/blood.2022018244 [M]:**
  uses chemo signatures to track therapy-related evolution — an
  application, not a general deconvolution method.
- **"Timing the Initiation of Multiple Myeloma," Nat Commun 2020(?),
  10.1038/s41467-020-15740-9 [M]:** timing-of-initiation from signature
  accumulation; adjacent, disease-specific.
- **TrackSig**, "Reconstructing evolutionary trajectories of mutation
  signature activities in cancer using TrackSig," Nat Commun 2020,
  10.1038/s41467-020-14352-7 [M] (+ preprint 10.1101/260471 [M]): CNV-
  based changepoint timing of signature activities — the nearest
  methodological neighbor; CNV-stratified rather than treatment/timing
  deconvolution from the raw catalog.
- **Oesophageal adenocarcinoma signature dynamics**, Nat Commun 2023,
  10.1038/s41467-023-39957-6 [M]; **colorectal geographic/age variation**,
  Nature 2025, 10.1038/s41586-025-09025-8 [M] — application-level timing/
  variation analyses.
- **Negative searches (documented, remain [U]):** "N-of-1-time" returned
  zero relevant records on OpenAlex (quoted phrase) AND Crossref
  (bibliographic query) — GPS timing, a 1981 cerebral-processes paper,
  etc. ClockShares returned nothing on two phrasings (CLOCK/SBS1/SBS5
  share-separation query). Both remain [U]-carried: known
  MutationalPatterns-ecosystem/community tools whose function is
  corroborated by the repo corpus but invisible to the backends used. If
  either does treatment-timing deconvolution generically, it could erode
  the (b) below — both must be read before printing "first."

### Verdict recommendation: SPLIT — (c) for TSB/RTT reporting; (b) for treatment/timing deconvolution

Reasoning: the corpus's "near-zero competition" note was [U]-carried and
half-wrong: per-signature TSB/RTT analysis is a developed subfield
(TensorSignatures, SigProfilerTopography, Topography 2023, Bergstrom 2018,
Zito-Xue-Miller). For treatment/timing deconvolution from mutation
catalogs as a general, model-based capability, only application-level
studies and CNV-based TrackSig surfaced; a generic per-sample
treatment/timing deconvolution claim survives as (b), conditional on
resolving the two backend-invisible tools (N-of-1-time, ClockShares) by
direct documentation fetch. **Negative results (N-of-1-time, ClockShares
not surfaced) are supportive, not conclusive — and here they are weaker
than usual, because the tools are known to exist by name.**
